newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel unions confirm July 23 strike.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel unions confirm July 23 strike.

text.p: French trade unions at Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc confirmed on Thursday they would stage a one-day strike on Wednesday, July 23.
The unions also rejected a management offer to meet on July 29 to discuss their demands for higher salaries, bonuses and a reduction in the working week to 35 hours from 37.5.
The unions told a news conference they wanted management to call a general assembly of personnel on July 21.
The union leaders also denounced a letter to staff from director-general Georges-Christian Chazot describing their action as irresponsible.
"The strike is already having an impact, customers are asking questions and we have registered cancellations," Chazot told Reuters.
Following the unions' refusal to wait until July 29 for a meeting with management, Chazot pleaded for "a minimum of time so that dialogue can begin".
The strike would be the first daylong strike at the tunnel, where a two-hour strike was held on November 18 just hours before a blaze inside the tunnel severely curtailed its operations.
